_readme: Olympique Lyonnais men's first team, season-by-season, 2000-01 to 2025-26. Compiled from Wikipedia (EN/FR), RSSSF, UEFA.com and other secondary sources via web search (direct WebFetch to wikipedia.org/fbref.com/etc. was blocked in this research environment, so all data was gathered via search-engine snippets rather than full page fetches). Numeric fields left as null were NOT confidently verified in this session and should not be treated as authoritative - see '_dataQualityNotes'. Cup-round detail ('coupeDeFrance','coupeDeLaLigue') is verified only for the seasons noted; other seasons are marked 'Unknown' rather than guessed.
_dataQualityNotes: Fully verified Ligue 1 numeric records (played/W/D/L/GF/GA/points) exist for 20 of 26 seasons: 2000-01, 2002-03 through 2004-05, 2006-07 through 2019-20, 2021-22, 2022-23.
2001-02: position and points (1st, 66 pts) confirmed; exact W/D/L/GF/GA not confirmed in available sources this session (left null).
2005-06: W/D/L and points confirmed (25W-9D-4L, 84 pts); GF/GA not confirmed (left null).

2020-21: final position (4th) is a moderate-confidence recollection, NOT independently search-verified this session; full match record left null. European campaign is well-verified: Lyon did not qualify for Europe that season (first miss since 1997), following a 7th-place finish in the COVID-curtailed 2019-20 season.
2023-24: final league position (6th) is search-verified; full match record not verified (left null). Coupe de France runner-up (lost final 1-2 to PSG) is verified.

2024-25 and 2025-26: only partial/low-confidence data could be gathered before this session's web-search quota was exhausted. Final league positions/points for both seasons are NOT reliably confirmed and are left null - treat any position implied elsewhere as unverified. Known verified facts: Lyon played UEFA Europa League in both seasons (reached the quarter-finals in 2024-25, losing 7-6 on aggregate to Manchester United; reached the round of 16 in 2025-26, losing to Celta Vigo), and Lyon qualified for the UEFA Champions League third qualifying round for 2026-27, implying a strong 2025-26 league finish.

IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO TASK BRIEF: the premise that 'OL reached the Europa League final in 2023-24, losing to Olympiacos' is FACTUALLY INCORRECT and was not used. Olympiacos beat Fiorentina in the 2024 UEFA Europa Conference League final (a different competition/final entirely); Lyon was not involved. In 2023-24 Lyon did not play in any European competition at all (verified). Lyon's real notable recent European run was reaching the Europa League quarter-finals in 2024-25 (lost to Manchester United 7-6 on aggregate over two legs, a 9-goal second-leg thriller).

Manager attributions for 2000-01 through 2022-23 are search-verified (including the mid-season Bosz->Blanc change in 2022-23). Manager attributions for 2023-24 through 2025-26 are lower-confidence (general knowledge, not individually re-verified this session): 2023-24 saw multiple changes (Laurent Blanc departed, brief Fabio Grosso spell, then Pierre Sage from December 2023); Pierre Sage is believed to have continued into 2024-25; the 2025-26 manager could not be confirmed. These should be spot-checked before publishing to end users.

Coupe de France and Coupe de la Ligue round-by-round results are Unknown (unverified) for most seasons except title/runner-up years, which are well-established facts. The Coupe de la Ligue existed through the 2019-20 season and was then discontinued (marked 'Competition discontinued' from 2020-21 onward).

European round reached is unverified ('Unknown') for a few seasons: 2000-01 (played UEFA Cup, exact round unconfirmed), 2002-03 (played Champions League, exact round unconfirmed), 2011-12, 2012-13 (unconfirmed), 2014-15 (confirmed Europa League play-off round entry only, not how far they progressed).

Aggregate club-level totals in 'club.aggregateApprox' are computed ONLY from the 20 fully-verified Ligue 1 seasons listed above; they exclude cup and European matches entirely and exclude the 6 seasons with incomplete data, so they meaningfully understate true totals since 2000. Treat as a partial/approximate figure, not a full competitive record.

seasons.europeanCup: UEFA Cup - Unknown round (unverified)
seasons.notes: Runners-up in Division 1, one point off champions Nantes. Coupe de la Ligue win per well-established general knowledge (final played April 2001); not individually re-verified via search this session.

seasons.europeanCup: Champions League - Group Stage, dropped to UEFA Cup - Round of 16 (4th round)
seasons.notes: Lyon's first-ever French top-flight title, won on the final day with a 3-1 win over Lens (who had led the table). Start of a record run of seven consecutive Ligue 1 titles (2001-02 to 2007-08). Full match record (W/D/L/GF/GA) not confirmed this session.

seasons.europeanCup: Champions League - Unknown exact round (unverified)
seasons.notes: Second consecutive title, ahead of Monaco (67 pts).

seasons.europeanCup: Champions League - Quarter-final (drew 2-2 agg. with Porto, eliminated; beat Real Sociedad in Round of 16)
seasons.notes: Third consecutive title, finished 3 points ahead of PSG.

seasons.europeanCup: Champions League - Quarter-final
seasons.notes: Fourth consecutive title, 12 points clear of Lille.

seasons.europeanCup: Champions League - Quarter-final
seasons.notes: Fifth consecutive title. GF/GA not confirmed this session.

seasons.europeanCup: Champions League - Round of 16
seasons.notes: Sixth consecutive title. Houllier's last season in charge (left 25 May 2007).

seasons.europeanCup: Champions League - Round of 16
seasons.notes: Seventh and final consecutive Ligue 1 title, capping the 2001-02 to 2007-08 run. Domestic treble (Ligue 1 + Coupe de France + Coupe de la Ligue), Lyon's most decorated single season. Coupe de France final win over PSG.

seasons.europeanCup: Champions League - Round of 16
seasons.notes: The seven-title streak ended; Bordeaux won Ligue 1. Lyon finished 3rd, 9 points off the top.

seasons.europeanCup: Champions League - Semi-final (lost to Bayern Munich; beat Real Madrid in Round of 16)
seasons.notes: Best-ever Champions League run: knocked out holders/eventual finalists' path via Real Madrid in the last 16, lost to Bayern Munich in the semi-final.

seasons.europeanCup: Champions League - Round of 16 (lost to Real Madrid)
seasons.notes: Puel's final season in charge.

seasons.europeanCup: Unknown (unverified)
seasons.notes: Domestic cup double (Coupe de France + Coupe de la Ligue) despite a mid-table-ish 4th place league finish. Garde's first season in charge.

seasons.europeanCup: Unknown (unverified)
seasons.notes: Finished 3rd behind champions PSG and Marseille.

seasons.europeanCup: Europa League - Quarter-final (lost to Juventus, after exiting Champions League play-off round vs Real Sociedad)
seasons.notes: Garde's final season in charge.

seasons.europeanCup: Europa League - entered via play-off round (round reached not confirmed)
seasons.notes: Runners-up to PSG (83 pts). Alexandre Lacazette top scorer in Ligue 1 with 27 goals (31 in all competitions).

seasons.manager: Hubert Fournier (until Dec 2015), then Bruno Génésio (from 24 Dec 2015)
seasons.europeanCup: Champions League - Group Stage
seasons.notes: Moved from Stade de Gerland to the new Parc Olympique Lyonnais (Groupama Stadium) mid-season; first match there was 9 January 2016 vs Troyes.

seasons.europeanCup: Champions League - Group Stage, dropped to Europa League - Semi-final (lost to Ajax, 5-4 on aggregate)
seasons.notes: Best Europa League run since re-entering continental competition after dropping from the Champions League group.

seasons.europeanCup: Europa League - Round of 16 (lost to CSKA Moscow on away goals, 3-3 agg.)
Champions League - Round of 16 (lost to Barcelona, 5-1 agg.)

seasons.manager: Sylvinho (start of season), then Rudi Garcia (from Oct 2019)
seasons.europeanCup: Champions League - Semi-final (beat Juventus in Round of 16 and Manchester City in Quarter-final, lost to Bayern Munich in Semi-final)
seasons.notes: Ligue 1 season curtailed after 28 games due to COVID-19; final standings decided on points-per-game, PSG declared champions. Lyon's 7th-place finish meant they missed European qualification for 2020-21 for the first time since 1997, despite reaching the Champions League semi-final that same season (played out in August 2020 due to the pandemic delay).

seasons.europeanCup: Did not qualify for European competition (first miss since 1997)
seasons.notes: Position (4th, behind champions Lille, PSG and Monaco) is a moderate-confidence recollection, not independently search-verified this session; full match record not confirmed - treat as unverified pending a follow-up check.

seasons.europeanCup: Europa League - Quarter-final (lost to West Ham United)
seasons.notes: Raw record produced 62 points; finished with 61 after a 1-point deduction imposed by the LFP over crowd trouble in the home match vs Marseille (21 Nov 2021, Payet bottle-throwing incident).

seasons.manager: Peter Bosz (until 9 Oct 2022), then Laurent Blanc (from 10 Oct 2022)
seasons.europeanCup: Did not qualify for European competition
seasons.notes: Final season of Jean-Michel Aulas's ~three-decade presidency; American businessman John Textor took over ownership/presidency during the season.

seasons.manager: Fabio Grosso (start of season, brief), then Pierre Sage (from Dec 2023)
seasons.europeanCup: Did not qualify for European competition
seasons.notes: Lyon had one of the worst starts to a Ligue 1 season in the club's history before a major turnaround under Pierre Sage, finishing 6th and reaching the Coupe de France final. That runner-up finish secured a Europa League berth for 2024-25 (PSG, the Coupe de France winner, qualified for Europe via the league instead). Full league match record and exact managerial start date not confirmed this session - flagged as lower confidence.

seasons.manager: Pierre Sage (believed, not independently re-verified this session)
seasons.europeanCup: Europa League - Quarter-final (lost to Manchester United, 7-6 on aggregate, after a 9-goal second leg at Old Trafford, 17 Apr 2025)
seasons.notes: Final league position/points could not be reliably confirmed before this session's search quota was exhausted; only mid-season (~March 2025) standings were found (4th place, 47 pts from 27 games). The club faced a high-profile DNCG (French football financial regulator) sanction threat over financial fair play in this season, which is worth separately verifying if precise financial/sporting-sanction details are needed.

seasons.europeanCup: Europa League - Round of 16 (lost to Celta Vigo, reported ~20 March 2026)
seasons.notes: Final Ligue 1 position/points for this season could NOT be confirmed - search quota was exhausted before this could be verified. The only strong signal found is that Lyon qualified for the UEFA Champions League third qualifying round for 2026-27, implying a competitive top-half finish, but the exact final table position is unconfirmed and must not be treated as known. Flagged as the single biggest remaining data gap in this dataset.

club.foundedNote: Formed in May 1950 by members who split from Lyon Université Club; the wider 'Olympique Lyonnais' name/lineage traces informally back to 1899-1901, but 1950 is the club's own recognized founding date.

stadiums.name: Stade de Gerland
stadiums.note: Home for the entire 2000-01 to first half of 2015-16 seasons; last competitive match there was early January 2016.

stadiums.name: Parc Olympique Lyonnais (Groupama Stadium)
stadiums.note: Located in Décines-Charpieu; first match 9 January 2016 vs Troyes (2015-16 Ligue 1, matchday 20). Sponsor name 'Groupama Stadium' applies from 2017; referred to generically as 'Parc OL'.

aggregateApprox.scope: Ligue 1 league matches only, for the 20 of 26 seasons (2000-01 to 2025-26) with fully verified match records in this dataset. EXCLUDES all cup and European matches, and excludes 2001-02, 2005-06 (partial), 2020-21, 2023-24, 2024-25, 2025-26.
aggregateApprox.note: This is a deliberately partial, approximate figure - NOT a full 2000-2026 competitive record. True all-competitions totals since 2000 would be meaningfully higher and were not computable from the sources reachable in this session.

sources: Note: direct WebFetch access to wikipedia.org, fbref.com, rsssf.org, transfermarkt.com and other football-data sites was blocked by this session's network egress policy; all figures above were extracted from Google/web-search result snippets referencing these sources rather than from direct page fetches, which increases the chance of small transcription errors. Recommend a follow-up pass with direct page access to fully verify, especially the flagged/null fields.
